cards.explanation: The answer is at the right hand of God's throne in heaven. The writer says Jesus took His seat at the right hand of the throne of the Majesty in heaven (Hebrews 8:1). He is the high priest we really do have, friends, seated in heaven.

The answer is False. The sanctuary and true tabernacle where Jesus ministers was “…set up by the Lord, not by man.” (Hebrews 8:2) The writer states it plainly, friends. This one wasn't built by a crew with hammers.

The answer is to offer both gifts and sacrifices. The writer says “…every high priest is appointed to offer both gifts and sacrifices…” (Hebrews 8:3) It's the reason he says Jesus needed something to offer too. A priest without an offering would be like me showing up with an empty cookie box.

The answer is False. The writer says if Jesus were on earth, He would not be a priest, because there are already priests here who offer gifts according to the law (Hebrews 8:4). Jesus has received a much more excellent ministry, the writer says in verse 6, friends.

The answer is a copy and shadow of what is in heaven. The writer says the place where they serve is “…a copy and shadow of what is in heaven.” (Hebrews 8:5) A copy points to the real thing without being the real thing, friends. The real thing is what is in heaven.

The answer is the pattern shown him on the mountain. Moses, Israel's leader, was warned, “…make everything according to the pattern shown you on the mountain.” (Hebrews 8:5) The warning came when he was about to build the tabernacle, bakers.

The answer is True. The writer says Jesus has received a more excellent ministry, “…just as the covenant He mediates is better and is founded on better promises.” (Hebrews 8:6) Better ministry, better covenant, better promises, friends. And we haven't even gotten to the promises yet.

The answer is people. The writer says, “But God found fault with the people…” (Hebrews 8:8) That's who God found fault with, friends. Verse 7 adds that if the first covenant had been without fault, no place would have been sought for a second.
The answer is True. God says, “…I will make a new covenant with the house of Israel and with the house of Judah.” (Hebrews 8:8) Those are His words, plain as day, friends. Both houses are named.

The answer is that they did not abide by it. God says, “…they did not abide by My covenant…” (Hebrews 8:9) That's why He says the new one won't be like it, friends. It's a heavy line, and the text doesn't say more than that.

The answer is in their minds and on their hearts. God says, “I will put My laws in their minds and inscribe them on their hearts.” (Hebrews 8:10) The laws go on the inside, friends. I think that's the part that gets me every time.

The answer is that He'll be their God and they'll be His people. God says, “And I will be their God, and they will be My people.” (Hebrews 8:10) That's a relationship, not a roster, friends. Short sentence, huge promise.

The answer is False. God says, “…they will all know Me, from the least of them to the greatest.” (Hebrews 8:11) It isn't only the greatest, friends. Everybody in the covenant, from the least to the greatest, gets to know Him.

The answer is that He will remember them no more. God says, “For I will forgive their iniquities and will remember their sins no more.” (Hebrews 8:12) Forgiveness is the promise, friends. Read it slowly, then read it again.

The answer is that it will soon disappear. The writer says, “…what is obsolete and aging will soon disappear.” (Hebrews 8:13) He says it right after saying the new covenant made the first one obsolete, friends. So the answer is right there in the verse.
